purpose: Immutable event contract for the Git-tracked canonical claim ledger.

field_semantics.event_type: Lifecycle operation applied to one canonical claim.
field_semantics.occurred_at: Timezone-aware ISO 8601 project timestamp recording when the lifecycle event occurred.
field_semantics.actor: Human or controlled system identity responsible for the event.
field_semantics.previous_event_id: Previous event for the same canonical claim. Null only for claim_created.
field_semantics.payload: Event-specific immutable data required to replay canonical claim state.
field_semantics.creation_provenance: Immutable audit snapshot recording how a canonical claim entered persistent knowledge.

rules: Every canonical claim begins with exactly one claim_created event.
claim_created always creates a claim in needs_review status.
Every claim_created event must preserve creation provenance. Research-evidence promotion must reference approved evidence snapshots; manual promotion must preserve a non-empty rationale.

Every new v0.5 research-evidence snapshot uses source_contract_version 0.1.0 and freezes Document identity, SHA-256 content hash, excerpt, context, location, reviewer, review time, and run provenance.
Legacy evidence snapshots without source_contract_version remain readable but new writers must not emit them.
A claim becomes active only through claim_reviewed.
Events are append-only; existing ledger lines are never mutated by normal lifecycle operations.
Every event after claim_created must reference the immediately preceding event for the same claim.
Event replay, not mutable ledger rows, determines current canonical claim state.
Automatic freshness expiry is derived from next_review_at and does not require a ledger event merely because the date passed.
claim_superseded does not delete the older claim.
Contradiction is represented by an independent contradicts relationship and does not implicitly change lifecycle.
A material factual replacement is represented by a new canonical claim plus an explicit supersedes relationship and a controlled claim_superseded lifecycle event, not by rewriting claim text.
occurred_at must include timezone information.
Canonical claim IDs and event IDs must remain stable across runtime index rebuilds.
Lifecycle events must follow the allowed previous-status transitions declared by their event type.
For claim_created, as_of may be earlier than created_at because historical real-world facts may enter canonical knowledge after the period they describe.
Canonical claim review provenance uses scope 'claim'. Document-level scope semantics belong to Temporal Knowledge document review, not Canonical Claim review.
claim_marked_historical and claim_contradicted are read-only v0.4 compatibility event types; v0.5 writers must not emit them.
Legacy claim_marked_historical projects to archived.
Legacy claim_contradicted projects to archived and may produce independent contradicts relationships from its target references.
claim_source_upgraded appends a validated v0.5 source snapshot without rewriting immutable creation provenance or changing lifecycle status.
